text:
Verified reference: **CATS: Cluster-Aware Thompson Sampling for Negative Mining in Sequential Recommendation**, Giulia Di Teodoro, Federico Siciliano, Nicola Tonellotto, Fabrizio Silvestri; SIGIR 2026, pp. 280–289; DOI **10.1145/3805712.3809539**. The identifier **11573/1775773** resolves to its institutional repository record. CATS combines item clustering with Thompson sampling: same-cluster candidates are considered more prone to false negatives, while nearby clusters can supply informative hard negatives. Sampling probability from the positive item’s cluster decays during training. [Verified record and abstract](https://iris.uniroma1.it/handle/11573/1775773).

Evidence supports treating similar unobserved items as **uncertain candidates**, rather than confirmed dislikes. CATS reports NDCG@10 improvements exceeding 20% over vanilla sampling and 16% over advanced sampling methods across SASRec, BERT4Rec, BSARec and MovieLens-1M, Amazon Beauty, BeerAdvocate. These are abstract-reported results, not evidence of gains for HSTU or the four target categories. Earlier work, [Trading Hard Negatives and True Negatives (IJCAI 2022)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.11752), likewise identifies the trade-off between informative hard negatives and false negatives. Practical inference: similarity can motivate cautious sampling or reduced negative penalties; it cannot establish a candidate’s true label. Neither source directly validates a particular “unlabeled competitor” loss.
